# Git Commit Instructions

When creating a commit message for this repository:

- Start with one conventional type: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `chore`, `ci`, `build`, or `perf`.
- Use this format: `<type>: <simple one-line title>`.
- Keep the title concise, specific, and written in the imperative mood.
- Add a body only when context is genuinely needed; use no more than 2–3 short lines.
- Do not add a body for a small, self-explanatory change.
- Do not include unrelated changes in the same commit.

Examples:

```text
feat: add monthly budget route
fix: prevent local D1 from using production config
refactor: simplify health check handler
```
